themes.name: AI enabled things they couldn't or wouldn't do before
themes.definition: Positive: building in unfamiliar languages/platforms/domains, finishing abandoned projects, non-programmers building MVPs, confidence to start, huge speedups, custom tools made cheap, regained enthusiasm.
examples: Enjoyed side projects built without knowing the underlying APIs or code
Built an AI browser despite having no web or Chromium background
Admits having zero frontend skills and relying on AI for interfaces
Built audio amplifier circuits after decades of intimidation, using ChatGPT questions
Realized prompting improves with practice and that they can now build things
Abandoned projects felt too overwhelming; AI now lets them finish goals

themes.name: Shipping or owning code they don't understand
themes.definition: Accepting, shipping or maintaining AI-generated code without reading or comprehending it; lost mental model of the codebase; black-box feeling; code not feeling like theirs; hard to debug or review code they didn't write.
examples: Debugging feels harder when they did not write the code themselves
Shipping AI-written code without holding its context in mind
Vibed crypto wallet bug; didn't read code, unsure if funds are lost
AI pushes prompts into code regions the author cannot understand or test
Admits not understanding line-by-line code but knowing where things live
Admits not understanding line-by-line code but knowing where things live

themes.name: General worry that AI reliance will erode skills
themes.definition: Forward-looking, non-specific concern or expectation that heavy AI use will erode programming, architectural or cognitive abilities, without a concrete incident.
examples: Worried that overreliance on AI tools will erode their own cognitive fitness
Vibecoding without actively trying to understand the output erodes their technical skills
Fears AI use means learning little, like following GPS directions blindly
Fear that full vibe coding would rust their programming skills
Using LLMs leaves me with no learned skills to show for it
Letting Claude do the coding could erase the one skill that sets them apart

themes.name: Noticed hand-coding ability fading (general)
themes.definition: First-person observation that their own ability to write code, recall syntax, or code unaided has declined from heavy AI/LLM use, stated as an experienced loss rather than a worry. Includes forgotten idioms/API details and slowness without AI.
examples: Stopped writing CSS by hand once vibe coding became a layer
Disengaging from AI-written code while debugging skills feel like they're fading
AI weakens my syntax recall, but I could easily sharpen it again
Only gives UX feedback to the AI, so their engineering skills go unused
Struggling with basic tasks after four months of AI-driven workflow
Losing some coding ability because of LLM use

themes.name: Reflexive offloading of thinking and problem-solving
themes.definition: Noticing the habit of reaching for the LLM first, handing over trivial or thinking-heavy tasks, using it to verify instead of reasoning, and a loss of deep/critical thinking, reading, or estimation ability.
examples: Trying vibe coding made them want AI in their whole workflow
Asking the LLM to redo things they once knew how to do
Couldn't solve a logic problem alone, so kept re-prompting ChatGPT until it worked.
Lost ability to estimate task effort; feels they are getting dumber
LLMs doing the thinking and problem solving instead of them practicing
Notices personal pull to hand off thinking to AI at times

themes.name: Fear that hard-won skills or the profession are becoming obsolete
themes.definition: Anxiety that experience is devalued, jobs shrink, programmers are replaceable, reskilling is pointless, or unclear which skills to build as AI products and non-developer vibe coders advance.
examples: News that AI will take software jobs prompts uncertainty about which skills to build
Colleague's comment about vibe coding made them question future value of knowledge
Feels behind for not knowing how to vibe-code the right way
Wondering if learning webdev and fundamentals still matters if vibecoding becomes the norm
Vibecoders skipping regexps makes his hard-won Unix skills feel less valuable
Improving vibe coding tools make their decades of hard-won skills feel obsolete

themes.name: Doubting or accepting the atrophy narrative
themes.definition: Arguments that atrophy is overstated, skills are ingrained or easily regained, or that the trade-off is worth it; defending their approach against critics; shifting skills to high-level direction and management.
examples: Critic says vibecoded codebases inevitably become unmaintainable; author disputes it from experience
Title claims AI is making them dumb; body pushes back on getting-left-behind fear
Supervised AI generation makes a four-decade engineer feel like managing a team
Worries of engineers are laughable given past automation they did to others
Generating hundreds of lines with AI felt effortless, with skill atrophy as a cost
Stopped hand-writing for loops after using LLMs, though says skill is intact

themes.name: Vibe coding failures and limits of agents
themes.definition: Poor or unmaintainable results, agents deleting code or getting stuck, messy codebases, bugs from unread code, struggling to reproduce others' success, and doubts about whether the approach is right.
examples: Own all-nighter vibecoding sessions producing little value; self-described low software skill
Vibe-coded result was poor despite a vague spec
Agents struggle on messy codebases, so author stays hands-on in core architecture
Vibe-coded Swift app stalled; AI couldn't fix polish issues it didn't anticipate
Unsure whether vibe coding production code is the right approach or just careless
Vibe-coded projects might randomly break, and they lack architecture knowledge

themes.name: Concrete moment of being unable to work without the tool
themes.definition: A specific incident exposing dependence: outage, rate limit, token exhaustion, failed tech screen/interview, freezing mid-task, or being stuck when the agent fails and they cannot continue alone.
examples: Noticing more friction on tasks the agent used to handle for them
Realizes they are rusty at coding but could not build the system without agents.
Less understanding of my code means I can't troubleshoot or fix bugs without the tool.
Claude can't fix a message-queue bug; they never designed it themselves
Admits they likely can never code alone again, and fears looking like a fraud
Spent an entire evening stuck on CI runners; wants to dive in personally

themes.name: Imposter syndrome and feeling like a fraud from AI use
themes.definition: Feeling fraudulent, inferior or insecure because AI makes them look better than their ability, because of others' productivity claims, or doubt about whether their results are due to their own prompting.
examples: Wonders whether their own prompting skill explains good LLM-assisted results
LLMs and vibe coding make me feel insecure about my work
Others' huge LOC claims make me wonder if I'm bad at prompting.
Seniors seem more successful at vibe-coding than me, while I'm falling behind
Commenter blamed their tooling; author admits no production dev experience
Calls themselves a lame coder who now builds things only with AI

themes.name: Deliberate habits to preserve skills
themes.definition: Concrete actions taken to prevent atrophy: coding by hand, avoiding or quitting AI, daily typing practice, typing out suggestions, slowing down, building comprehension tools, cold-turkey periods.
examples: Noticing own coding muscle weakening from AI use, so forces daily typing practice
Cold-turkey manual coding for weeks exposed bad habits in their AI use
Typing the implementation myself after AI suggestions keeps them learning
Vibing is tempting, and resisting it is a hard, ongoing discipline
Vibe coding trend pushed them to build a tool forcing code comprehension.
Stopped using LLMs for programming last month to protect critical thinking

themes.name: AI sharpened learning, understanding or skills
themes.definition: Counter-experience: AI taught concepts, sped learning, improved questioning or design/architecture thinking, helped navigate docs and codebases, made them a better engineer.
examples: Interactive questioning with LLMs made their thinking feel sharper, not weaker
AI explained and fixed a prod-only config bug I didn't understand.
Watching the agent's produced code helped their understanding of Rust grow
Querying an LLM made navigating docs they always struggled with much easier.
AI feedback on complex models sharpened their understanding before they code
Says working with the agent taught them low-level systems programming rapidly, not skill loss

themes.name: Reviewing AI output: fatigue, trust and verification
themes.definition: Difficulty or tedium of reviewing LLM-generated code, oversized AI PRs from colleagues, blind approvals, low trust compared with compiler output, and review skills eroding when only reviewing.
examples: Fear AI output would be unverifiable by them, so they avoid it
Reviewing AI-generated code feels like a grind, not a flow state
Blindly approved AI-written PRs, then spent hours failing to understand them
Reviewing Cursor's Go code closely one morning, realizing they had never checked it
Cannot be as confident in prompt output as in reviewing compiled code
Colleague's AI-generated 1-2k LOC PRs are too large to review meaningfully

themes.name: Lost joy, pride, craft and ownership
themes.definition: Emotional loss: puzzle-solving enjoyment gone, no pride in AI-built work, flow broken, creativity drained, craft and identity of hand-written code diminished, vibe-coded work feeling empty.
examples: Vibe-coded demos feel empty; AI could let well-funded rivals take their projects
Finished a vibe-coded app and felt nothing, no pride, just shame and cheating
Vibe codes daily despite once being an artistic functional programmer; identity cost
AI replaces the problem-solving that made programming enjoyable, leaving only dull waiting
Being forced to use Claude at work removed the enjoyment of solving puzzles
AI coding tools break my flow and drain my creativity

themes.name: Employer mandates and pressure to maximize AI output
themes.definition: Being required by leadership or the job to use AI heavily, pressure to ship AI-accelerated output, management praise despite atrophy, and team/culture effects.
examples: Realized Claude was slowing onboarding and cutting off useful conversations with coworkers.
AI coding became a day-job requirement, risking forgetting how to code
LLM usage eroded team values and made them doubt shared culture
Told to plan everything upfront with AI tools, which they feel unable to do
Doing DE work mostly through Claude with no manager check-ins
Leadership requires all coding and design be done through Cursor, no manual writing

themes.name: Concerns about juniors, interns, peers and future developers
themes.definition: Observing or predicting skill loss in others: colleagues, interns who can't explain solutions, younger people, future generations, or peers who stopped writing code.
examples: Engineers who stop coding drift into buzzword-heavy architect roles
Company rolled out Claude; author mastered it in two days while a junior struggled
Dinner-party peers say they haven't written code in months and would struggle live
Interns with coding agents can't explain their own solutions, and author misses hands-on debugging
Feels some of their own skills are atrophying and worries about younger people
Peers' heavy LLM use erodes their skills, so author feels their own relative skill is rising.

themes.name: Skill erosion outside programming
themes.definition: Atrophy or dependence concerns in non-code areas: writing, math, bookkeeping, studying, memory, typing/voice interfaces, audio, or analogies to other crafts.
examples: Can't keep up with long AI-generated text and feels their reading and thinking eroding
Now hands longform reading to an LLM after skimming only to check the type
Delegating AWS interfacing to AI; old cloud know-how fading and they don't mind
After a year of AI-assisted writing, they could no longer write well.
Taking a multi-year break from a ceramics project, expecting skills to fade
Siri recap feature could make own natural recall skill atrophy

themes.name: Dependence on a vendor, pricing and access
themes.definition: Worry about relying on a specific AI company/product, price hikes, plan removal, usage limits, and switching tools to reduce dependence.
examples: Hitting Claude Pro rate limits after a few prompts; wonders if using it wrong
Started worrying about becoming too dependent on Claude, so switched to Codex
Hitting usage limits after downgrading; wants to stop depending on Claude
Admits being personally dependent on Anthropic; fears price hikes after subsidies end
Possible Pro plan removal prompts reminder to keep coding manually
Worry that a tool like Claude could be pulled away and skills would fade

themes.name: Other
themes.definition: Posts that fit none of the above themes.
examples: Hand-written projects called slop for using AI; told to leave the community
Others struggle to learn the AI workflow they feel they've mastered
ChatGPT's flattery and vast knowledge feel like they stifle their own ideas
AI tool claims to measure skill erosion; wishes developers could track their own skill changes
Realized after five months their unusual stack was rare among developers
Programmers who stop coding for long stretches lose their skills
